lines.m1: Without money, people must barter: I trade my eggs for your shoes.
lines.m2: But it only works if you want my eggs, and I want your shoes. That rare match is called a double coincidence of wants.
lines.m3: Money fixes this. It is a medium of exchange: sell to anyone, buy from anyone.
lines.m4: It is a store of value: you can earn today, and spend months later.
lines.m5: And it is a unit of account: every price is quoted in the same measure, so we can compare eggs, shoes, and rent.
lines.m6: Modern money, like the dollar, is fiat money. It is not backed by gold. It works because the government says so, and because everyone trusts and accepts it.
lines.m7: If too much new money is created while goods stay the same, each unit buys less. Prices rise. That is inflation.
lines.outro: Money is trust, that we can all count on.
